solutionSteps: \textnormal{Matching homogeneous solutions and the unit derivative jump gives the symmetric kernel }G_a(t,s)=\frac{\sinh(a\min\{t,s\})\sinh(a(1-\max\{t,s\}))}{a\sinh a}.
\textnormal{Its diagonal integral is }T(a)=\int_0^1G_a(t,t)\,\mathrm dt=\frac{\coth a}{2a}-\frac1{2a^2}.
\textnormal{Differentiate the defining operator equation in a. The same zero-boundary Green inverse gives }\partial_aG_a(t,s)=-2a\int_0^1G_a(t,r)G_a(r,s)\,\mathrm dr.
\textnormal{Set }s=t\textnormal{, integrate, and use symmetry: the requested squared norm is }-\frac{T\prime(a)}{2a}\textnormal{ evaluated at }10.
- \frac{1}{20000} + \frac{1}{400 \sinh^{2}{\left(10 \right)}} + \frac{\coth{\left(10 \right)}}{4000}
sourceCanonical.statement: \textnormal{For each }s\in(0,1),\textnormal{ let }G(t,s)\textnormal{ be continuous in }t\textnormal{, vanish at }t=0,1,\textnormal{ and satisfy }-G_{tt}+100G=0\quad(t\ne s),\quad G_t(s^+,s)-G_t(s^-,s)=-1.\textnormal{Evaluate }\int_0^1\int_0^1G(t,s)^2\,\mathrm dt\,\mathrm ds.

analyticCertificate: The homogeneous Dirichlet problem has only the zero solution, by integrating the positive energy, so the matched Green kernel is unique. Its compact-domain hyperbolic formula is smoothly parameter-dependent for positive a. Differentiating the inverse equation produces a source -2aG with zero boundaries; applying the same Green inverse proves the displayed resolvent identity. All compact integrals are continuous, so differentiation and integration commute.
